Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) is the principal staff element of the Secretary of Defense in the exercise of policy development, planning, resource management, and program evaluation responsibilities. OSD includes the Offices of the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense, Under Secretaries of Defense, Deputy Chief Management Officer, Assistant Secretaries of Defense, General Counsel, and the Director of Administration. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES), a small, elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. As a Senior Executive, you will influence the direction of innovation and transformation of the federal government and lead the next generation of public servants.
MajorDuties: As the Principal Director, the incumbent serves as the counterpart to the DASD(MC&FP) in providing policy guidance and program direction to Office of the DASD(MC&FP) Directors and administrative staff. The Principal Director assists the DASD with the following functions: Frames the Office of the DASD(MC&FP) strategic plan, based upon broad assessments and pragmatic evaluations of long-term organizational requirements. Exercises authority and responsibility for the full spectrum of strategic human capital management activities across the Military Community and Family Programs Functional Community. Represents the DASD(MC&FP) in high-level meetings, briefings and conferences with top level executives and managers from Congress, DoD, the Government Accountability Office, other federal agencies, departments and activities, private sector corporations and other business officials, and representatives of non-governmental entities. Identifies and negotiates decisions concerning major budget allocations and other critical matters necessary to accomplishment of the Office of the DASD(MC&FP) mission. Maintains professional contacts with high-level executives and representatives of industry partners, trade and professional associations, veterans and military service organizations, and special interest, constituent, and advocacy groups. Develops policies, conducts analyses, provides advice, makes recommendations and issues guidance on Defense plans and programs for military community and family issues in accordance with Defense Department force planning, major national objectives, and Administration policy. Reviews and evaluates programs to carry out approved policies and standards consistent with the requirements for the Military Family Readiness Council. Develops and executes a research agenda for military family readiness and quality of life programs to support analysis of the impact of activities and services, ensuring the findings are integrated into policy decisions and priorities.

Experience with major weapons systems contracts with large volume of government furnished equipment. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. You will facilitate execution of effective systems engineering processes for production, installation and test, fielding, and fleet support for combat systems and their associated elements.

You will provide key leadership to establish the vision for the future Surface Navy Combat Power capabilities and ensure there are continuing assessments of PEO IWS strategies, goals, and objectives.
You will direct efforts to foster success in meeting overall PEO IWS mission.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Eligibility will be based upon a clear showing the applicant has training, education and experience of the scope and quality sufficient to effectively carry-out the duties of the position. The individual must possess a broad point of view and an awareness and understanding of individual or organizational responsibilities in relation to DoD or government-wide strategic priorities. Executives should demonstrate ability to work with internal and external partners to support national security objectives. This perspective is typically gained through a variety of diverse work experiences. Inherent to this ECQ is the ability to establish an organizational vision and to implement it in a continuously changing environment.2) Leading People: This core qualification involves the ability to lead people toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. This position is in the Senior Executive Service (SES) which is a small elite group of top government leaders. SES members possess a diverse portfolio of experiences including strong skills to lead across organizations. MajorDuties: The Chief, Interagency and International Community of Practice works with the Director of Military Programs; the Commander, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers; the Assistant Secretary of the Army (Civil Works); the Deputy Under Secretary of the Army (International Affairs); and the Department of Defense (Office of the Secretary of Defense, Joint Chiefs of Staffs, Department of the Military Commanders and Chiefs), this position is responsible for developing and managing USACE corporate IIS strategic business initiatives. The position provides programmatic direction and assistance to all USACE headquarters offices, divisions, districts, laboratories, and other field offices to ensure timely and proper development and maintenance of HQUSACE IIS strategic planning and all supporting MSC plans. These plans must be integrated to ensure alignment of workload and workforce with USACE strategic planning. As Chief of the Interagency and International Services Community, the incumbent is the focal point for corporate IIS strategic planning for USACE and for program- level relationships with external stakeholders. In addition to developing USACE' s strategic alliance profile, this individua I is responsible for reimbursable support activities for non-DOD entities and international activities including in direct support of US forces; evaluating nationally significant reimbursable work; and providing non-reimbursable, nationally significant support to US agencies and international organizations. The range of technical expertise provided under this program spans all USACE competencies and skills including engineering, environmental, construction management, real estate, research and development, and related services. Formulates plans and strategies for USACE support to the National Security and National Military Strategies. Develops strategies for cooperation with developed nations and support for developing nations and emerging democracies.
